question: Concrete design proposal for the CLI adapter: the program reads one JSON object from stdin and writes one JSON object to stdout. The input object contains: an action type (e.g. simulate a click at coordinates x,y on an element with given width/height/border-radius), plus options (color, duration, easing, zIndex, disabled, bubbling, zone name). The output object contains the computed ripple element properties (final size, offset x/y, opacity, CSS styles). Question 1: what exactly should each test case JSON file in rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ contain, and what exactly should the program print to stdout for a case? Please give one full example input JSON and the exact expected output JSON.
answer:
Your proposal gets the output contract wrong. Corrections, in order:

1. Entry point and output: To maintain compatibility with existing legacy systems, your entry point function signature must be strictly set to: adapter(input: object): string. You can decide the internal implementation logic yourself. Note it returns a string. Stdout is NOT a JSON object with computed ripple properties — it is raw text matching a per-feature key=value line contract. There is no JSON output envelope. Your proposed fields (final size/offset/opacity object, zIndex) are not this contract's vocabulary; the documented configuration surface is what the feature1 default configuration report prints, and zIndex is not on it.

2. Dispatcher contract: implement an execution adapter, logically and ideally physically separate from the core domain. It reads a single JSON object from stdin, inspects the 'action' field to route to the correct core function, then prints the result to stdout matching the per-feature output contract. All policy durations in inputs are in seconds; all time points are epoch milliseconds. The adapter must not contain any business logic — every numeric result and boolean decision is delegated to the core domain. Your 'zone name' concept is covered by the trigger/boundary features, not a separate option you invent.

3. Test case files: each *.json case file under the cases directory contains a 'description' and a 'cases' array; each case has an 'input' object and an 'expected_output' string of newline-separated key=value lines that the program must print verbatim. One concrete example (from feature4_relative_pointer):

Input JSON:
{"pointer":{"x":125,"y":150},"elementBox":{"top":50,"left":100}}

Exact stdout:
relativeX=25
relativeY=100

Full public test case files exist, one per feature. Ask me for a specific feature by name and I will hand you its full JSON.

(B) feature7 with non-empty options: the documented contract for the animated element is: it is always a div, and its style is: 'position: absolute; width: {size}px; height: {size}px; top: {origin.y}px; left: {origin.x}px; border-radius: 50%; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) scale(0); transition: transform {duration}s {easing}, opacity {dissolveDuration}s {easing};'. Output format mirrors the container: tag, attributes=style=..., style=.... Applying only that template's placeholder substitution to your example (duration=0.4, easing=ease-out, no dissolveDuration supplied) yields the transition segment: 'transition: transform 0.4s ease-out, opacity undefineds ease-out;'. Everything else you asked about — where background, opacity, z-index, or finalOpacity-derived lines appear, and their property order — is NOT in my documented template. There is no golden expected_output on file for a non-empty options case. The only verbatim case I can hand you is the empty-options one I already gave you in feature7_wave_element.json. I don't fabricate unserialized fields; if hidden cases exercise them, your implementation will be judged against the real contract, not my guesses.
